chunks.rationale: test/threadView.test.tsx: two #555 regression tests. view() now takes optional onFetchDiff / onFetchReviewContext (empty-diff stub stays the default). Test 1 mounts Changes with a tall itinerary (hard-stop, author notes, ≥4 steps, files across ci-config/critical/tests/impl/docs) and walks from the commit textarea up to [aria-label=Changes] so wrapping the box in .changesScroll fails. Test 2 reads ThreadView.module.css per-rule-block and requires .commitBox flex-shrink:0 + sticky, .changesHead flex-shrink:0, .changesScroll overflow-y:auto + min-height:0, and no overflow:auto on .patchScroll.
risks: Test 1 is green before the JSX/CSS fix because .changesScroll does not exist yet; the ancestor walk is the durable guard once the wrapper lands.
Test 2 is expected red until the parallel CSS worker lands. node:test stops at the first assertion, so a partial CSS fix will surface the next missing declaration rather than all of them at once.
The .patchScroll guard is specifically overflow:auto (not overflow-y:auto). A nested-scroller regression that used overflow-y:auto would not trip it.
This worktree does not apply the ThreadView.tsx / ThreadView.module.css fix; those files are owned by a parallel worker. Merging tests first will keep the CSS layout test red until that worker lands.
jsdom has no layout, so Test 1 cannot assert clipping or sticky positioning — only DOM ancestry and CSS text.
